title: Ngorongoro Crater: A Visitor's Guide
excerpt: The Ngorongoro Crater is a collapsed volcano full of wildlife. What to expect on a crater day, and tips for making the most of it.
body:
The Ngorongoro Crater is the world's largest intact, unflooded volcanic caldera. Its floor is about 260 km² and lies roughly 600 m below the rim. Inside, wildlife lives in a natural enclosure, which makes it one of the best places in Africa for a single day of game viewing.

## What you can see

Lions, spotted hyenas, elephants (mainly old bulls), buffaloes, zebras, wildebeest, hippos and flamingos in the soda lake. Ngorongoro is also one of the best places in Tanzania to see [black rhinos](/blog/ngorongoro-rhinos/). There are no giraffes on the crater floor, as the steep walls are difficult for them.

## A crater day

Most visitors descend early in the morning and spend half a day or most of a day on the crater floor, with a picnic lunch at a designated site. There is a time limit for the crater floor per visit.

## Tips

- Start early: the light is better and there are fewer vehicles.
- Bring a warm jacket: the rim is high and cool.
- Watch out for kites at the picnic area; they steal food.
- Binoculars help for rhinos, which often stay at a distance.

## Where to stay

Lodges on the crater rim have spectacular views. Staying in Karatu is a good alternative. See [Karatu](/blog/karatu-guide/).

## Conservation Area

The crater is part of the larger Ngorongoro Conservation Area, where Maasai also live. See also [Empakaai and Olmoti](/blog/ngorongoro-highlands-empakaai/).

Read our [Ngorongoro page](/national-parks/ngorongoro/) or [plan your safari](/travel-proposal/).
